question.text: When calculating mutual fund holding-period returns for a period of less than one year, the convention is to show them as:

answer.text: Annualized returns using the CAGR formula

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook treats holding-period returns of less than one year as simple absolute returns from start NAV to end NAV. Annualising a few weeks or months of performance would assume the same rate continues for a full year, which the workbook explicitly discourages for short windows. The Trap: CAGR (option B) is appropriate for multi-year holding periods, not for sub-one-year periods. Inflation- and tax-adjusted returns are different return concepts and are not the default convention here. Note: Separately, SEBI's advertisement guideline carves out exceptions for schemes in existence between six and twelve months (simple annualised growth rate) and for money market / cash / liquid schemes (simple annualised yields over 7, 15 and 30 days). These exceptions apply to advertisements, not to the general holding-period return calculation in option A.
